name: Jerusalem artichoke (Sunchoke)

schedule.notes: Plant tubers 4 in deep. Plants grow to 8 to 10 ft. Pick your spot wisely — they're impossible to eradicate once established.
Lift after frost knocks down the tops. Frost dramatically improves flavor.

harvest.cues: Tops blackened by frost; tubers 1 to 3 in long, lumpy. Mulch heavily to harvest through winter.
harvest.storageNotes: Best left in the ground under mulch. Dig as needed. Once dug, fridge 1 to 2 weeks max — they dry quickly.

varieties.name: Stampede
varieties.notes: Fastest to maturity, large white tubers.

varieties.name: Red Fuseau
varieties.notes: Smooth, finger-shaped, red-skinned. Easier to clean than knobby types.

notes: Plant on the north edge of the garden — they shade everything south of them. Contains inulin, which is gas-producing for many people; cook well and start with small portions. Self-perpetuates from any leftover tuber fragment.
